description: spec injection works on every host: the template no longer overrides tool names, and the integration suite can run outside Linux/macOS
changelog:
**Fixed — spec injection was silently inert on any host whose tool names differ from Claude Code's.** The `spec_injection` section shipped ACTIVE in `.trellis/config.yaml` with a Claude-spelled `tools:` list (Read/Edit/Write/MultiEdit). An active section is a hard override, and one config ships to every platform, so on DSH — whose bridge forwards its own lowercase read/write/edit verbatim — every event failed the membership test and no spec was ever injected. It failed silently: no warning, no output, indistinguishable from "no spec governs this file".

The section now ships **fully commented out**, matching the `context_injection` section's long-standing precedent, so the hook's built-in default applies. That default now covers both spellings, because it is what decides the trigger whenever the config omits `tools:`. The unknown-name warning checks a separate known-name set (which also admits `apply_patch`, `glob`, `grep`), so it fires on a typo instead of on a host. `trellis.test.ts` pins both the commented-out block and the documented defaults.

**If you previously added a `tools:` list to `.trellis/config.yaml`, check its spelling.** An entry written for one platform disables injection on any other; omit the key unless you are deliberately narrowing the trigger set.

**Fixed — the spec-injection integration suite could not run on Windows or conda hosts.** The interpreter was hard-coded to `python3`, and the suite is wrapped in `describe.skipIf(!hasPython())`: on a host with only `python.exe` (Windows, or a conda/venv) every test **skipped**, so a green run meant "never executed" rather than "passed". The interpreter is now resolved from `TRELLIS_TEST_PYTHON` with a `python3` fallback. Subprocess output is also CRLF-normalized (Windows Python writes CRLF to a pipe, so comparisons failed on line endings), the harness strips `*_CONTEXT_ID` identity overrides (running the tests from inside a Trellis session exported `TRELLIS_CONTEXT_ID`, silently turning the stateless cases stateful), and the GC symlink-guard test is skipped on Windows, where creating a directory symlink needs Developer Mode. On this machine the suite went from 85 skipped to 83 passing with 3 platform-gated skips.

**Documentation** — `.trellis/spec/cli/backend/spec-injection.md` gains a test-harness section (interpreter resolution, CRLF, identity environment, symlinks) and records the new failure mode: a `tools:` list written for another host fails silently.
notes: No `--migrate` required; `migrations` is empty. Downstream projects pick the corrected `.trellis/config.yaml` template and the corrected hook default up on their next `trellis update`. Existing projects that added a `tools:` list of their own are unaffected by the template change (a locally modified config.yaml is hash-tracked and reported as a conflict, never overwritten) — but such a list is worth re-reading against this changelog, since it may be why injection appears dead on one of their platforms. The only other user-visible change is in Trellis's own test suite, which does not ship to projects.
